title: Transvaginal ultrasound
what: An ultrasound of the uterus and ovaries with a thin probe placed in the vagina. This shows the organs much better than through the belly.
why: For lower belly pain, period problems, when planning a pregnancy or in early pregnancy, or at a routine checkup.
tell_doctor: The date your last period started
If you have never had sex. Then the probe is not inserted, and the scan is done through the belly
If you are allergic to latex

prepare.title: Day of your cycle
prepare.text: It is usually done on day 5 to 7 of your cycle, right after your period. The doctor may choose another day.

prepare.title: Bladder
prepare.text: Go to the toilet before the scan. Your bladder should be empty.

prepare.title: Hygiene
prepare.text: A normal shower the evening before or in the morning. No special products are needed.

bring: A sheet or towel, if your clinic asks
steps: You undress below the waist and lie on the exam table with your knees bent
A single-use cover with gel is put on the probe
The doctor gently puts the probe a short way into the vagina
The probe is turned a little to see the uterus and ovaries
The probe is taken out, and you get dressed
feel: A feeling of pressure, usually without pain
If it is uncomfortable or painful, tell the doctor, and they will be more gentle
after: You can go back to your usual day right away
You usually get the report right away
A little discharge from the gel is normal

faq.q: Can I have a vaginal ultrasound during pregnancy?
faq.a: Yes, it is safe. In early pregnancy, this is the best way to see the pregnancy.

faq.q: Can I have an ultrasound during my period?
faq.a: Yes, if the doctor ordered it urgently. But for a routine checkup, right after your period is better.
